dispute_cards.reading_a: A duty exists only where a source span establishes the deontic operator for the act.
dispute_cards.reading_b: A duty may be inferred from the practical necessity of the act in its context.

dispute_cards.reading_a: Permission is a positive entitlement that must be established by a source span.
dispute_cards.reading_b: Permission follows from the mere absence of a prohibition on the act.

dispute_cards.reading_a: A prohibition is a positive ban that must be established by a source span.
dispute_cards.reading_b: A prohibition may be inferred from the absence of a permission for the act.

dispute_cards.reading_a: A definitional norm is a distinct normative family with its own boundary.
dispute_cards.reading_b: A definition is only a naming convention carried inside another family.

dispute_cards.reading_a: Competence is a power held by a named body and must be established by a source span.
dispute_cards.reading_b: Competence follows from the ordinary function of the body without a further span.

dispute_cards.reading_a: A condition is a guard on the norm and must be established as part of the norm.
dispute_cards.reading_b: A condition is a factual premise of the case and not part of the norm.

dispute_cards.reading_a: An exception defeats a norm only where the defeat is established by a source span.
dispute_cards.reading_b: An exception limits the scope of the norm from the start rather than defeating it.

dispute_cards.reading_a: The governing time is the qualification established for the norm itself.
dispute_cards.reading_b: The governing time follows the time the fact occurred.

negative_examples.non_claim: Nothing in this package lets a missing duty be read as a ban, or a ban as a missing duty.
An unproven claim stays Unknown; absence of a proven source span is never falsity.

non_claims: This package is not an adoption of normative semantics: no reading, card or verdict here is accepted.
It is non-authoritative: it cannot satisfy a requirement, promote a lifecycle or establish legal correctness.
No runtime surface exists or is promised: there is no normative IR, rule graph or applicability evaluator.
A corpus probe records only path, span, bytes and sha256; no legal text is copied and a probe is not a reading.
Every dispute card is unresolved or conflicted by construction: a verdict resolved is refused without a human source review.
The two negative examples are boundaries, not findings: absence of obligation is not prohibition and lack of evidence is not falsity.
Family labelling of a corpus probe is a coverage label, not a claim that the span states that family.
revision_policy: Re-derive before use: re-hash every tracked anchor, re-read the family order from the T01 register, re-probe the bounded corpus set and re-render; no timestamp and no aggregate engine hash are stored here.
